_doc: qAI named exclusions (qai.md §3). Every entry cites the rule it implements. Automatic tag matching alone is not allowed to decide membership where a structural exclusion applies; changes here are rule changes under §10 and need an anchored decision. Symbols already carried by keeper/paper-index.mjs's shared QX20_EXCLUDE set (stablecoins, wrapped majors, exchange tokens) are not repeated.

stablecoins.reason: §3: a stablecoin is not an AI asset however it is tagged.

wrappedOrBridged.reason: §3: a wrapped or bridged LISTING is a representation, not the asset. The issuer decides which listing is canonical; a third-party bridge's listing is out. wTAO carries no AI tag at all, so it is excluded structurally rather than by name.

stakingAndSubnetDerivatives.reason: §3: staking and derivative representations are out — a claim on stake inside a network is not an independent holding of that network.

memecoins.reason: §3: AI-tagged memecoins are excluded by default (the `memes-in` variant stays in the research CSV). A meme market belongs to the Meme rulebook, not here.

SN0.reason: §3: staked TAO ("Root"), a derivative of validator stake, not an independent asset. Named here because CoinGecko's `artificial-intelligence` category carries SN0 while the CMC cache never did — the name must not enter through the CoinGecko side of the intersection.

SN_SUBNETS.reason: §3: Bittensor dTAO subnet ("alpha") tokens — SN4, SN9, SN51, SN64 and the rest — are derivatives of validator stake within a subnet. CoinGecko lists them in `artificial-intelligence`; the CMC `bittensor-subnets` tag catches most, this pattern catches the rest.

RNDR.reason: §3 / one-listing-per-asset: RNDR is the superseded ticker of the same asset now listed as RENDER. Holding both would double-count one network.

AGIX.reason: §3 / one-listing-per-asset: SingularityNET's AGIX migrated into the Artificial Superintelligence Alliance token, which is listed as FET. Kept here so a stale listing cannot re-enter beside FET.
